title: Pro-etale direct image is left exact
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes and $A$ a commutative ring, and let $f_*:\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)\to\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ be the direct image of sheaves of modules on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image]. Then $f_*$ is additive and left exact: for every exact sequence $0\to F'\to F\to F''$ in $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ the sequence $0\to f_*F'\to f_*F\to f_*F''$ is exact in $\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$.

proof.text: For two module-sheaf morphisms $a,b:F\to G$, addition is addition on sections. By the formula for direct image on morphisms, for each $V\to Y$ one has $(f_*(a+b))_V=(a+b)_{V\times_YX}=a_{V\times_YX}+b_{V\times_YX}=(f_*a)_V+(f_*b)_V$. The same formula gives $f_*0=0$ on morphisms. Equality of sheaf morphisms is equality of all components, so $f_*$ is additive.

proof.text: Use the small-site/module-universe convention of the direct-image definition, so both module categories are abelian. Let $b:F\to G$ and put $K=\ker b$ in the category of $A_X$-module sheaves. Kernels of module sheaves are computed sectionwise. Thus for every $V\to Y$, $(f_*K)(V)=K(V\times_YX)=\{s\in F(V\times_YX):b_{V\times_YX}(s)=0\}=\ker((f_*b)_V)$. These identifications commute with restriction because each kernel has the restrictions induced from $F$. They respect the $A_Y(V)$-action because on both sides it is restriction of the $A_X(V\times_YX)$-action along the component $\rho^f_{A,V}:A_Y(V)\to A_X(V\times_YX)$ of the constant-ring structure map specified in the direct-image definition. The inclusion is on each object the kernel inclusion. Consequently $f_*K\to f_*F$ is the kernel of $f_*b$. Also $f_*$ sends the zero sheaf to the zero sheaf, since its value at every object is the zero module.

proof.text: Write the given sequence as $0\to F\xrightarrow{a}G\xrightarrow{b}H$, relabelling its three terms. In an abelian category its exactness says precisely that $a$ identifies $F$ with $\ker b$: $a$ is monic, and its image is $\ker b$. Let $c:F\xrightarrow{\sim}\ker b$ be this identification, so $a$ is $c$ followed by the kernel inclusion. A functor sends an isomorphism to an isomorphism, since it sends the two inverse identities to inverse identities. Applying $f_*$, step 2 therefore identifies $f_*a$ with the kernel inclusion of $f_*b$, up to the isomorphism $f_*c$. It is monic with image that kernel. Together with preservation of the zero sheaf, this is exactly the asserted exactness $0\to f_*F\to f_*G\to f_*H$.
